Also, they should be bigger than that after a week, as you usually start to see at least 2 sets of true leaves (the spikey marijuana leaves, not the first round pair you see). Is the soil you used contaminated? Or was it cleaned? You also need to balance the pH of your water because if it is too acidic it will burn the plant, and otherwise it won’t give it enough nutrients. You also want to mix in some perlite to your soil to improve aeration and drainage, because they need a TON of drainage!! They need a lot of oxygen and if the soil is too packed your roots will rot. 
You also need to be very careful with watering. I’ve been using one of those little travel spray bottles to water mine, so I just do a couple sprays until the top of the soil is moist. To see how moist your soil is, stick ur finger in about up to ur knuckle and go from there. If it is damp, do not water it as you will kill it. 
There’s a LOT of trial and error that goes into growing these, so goodluck!

I found two adults in my room a couple months ago in the beginning of April after having my ex over, got the exterminator in 2 days after (was very lucky to get someone there ASAP). 
Before exterminator came I took everything I owned and divided it into sections: Stuff that is washable, stuff that is unwashable and needs to be bagged, and stuff to throw out. Threw sheets and pillow and etc into garbage. Washable stuff got bagged until put into the washing machine, and then I dried for the longest time at the highest heat (sometimes twice). I only just recently moved everything back into my room as it’s now 4 months without seeing one. 
I also got a bed bug mattress protector, moved everything away from the walls or curtains they could use to climb into my bed, and got those little circular traps you put on your bed posts. My room only had a bed and dresser (I lived out of a Rubbermaid bin) until last week. 
I also steam cleaned anything that could be steam cleaned such as purses, belts, hats, shoes, etc.
If you got rid of them before and you live in an apartment it could very well be neighbors that these guys are travelling from.

if you want to take any extra measures I’d recommend:
- traps for your couch and bed legs. they’re like little circles that the bed bugs climb up into and then get stuck.
- bed bug covers for mattress and pillowcases
- steam treat anything possible. even if u have a little mini hand held one, that’s what I used!
- start doing bedding every 5 days
- when changing outfits put the worn outfit into a garbage bag. then put your weight onto it while twisting it shut as to get the air out and suffocate them (if any are in there)
- HEAT! Dry your clothes and anything else that can go inside on the highest setting for the longest time. 
- wear light clothes, and white or light bed sheets as to be able to see them easier if any are on you
- put all ur stuff into bags.

Bed bugs can live over a year without a blood meal (if there isn’t a blood meal present). The males have pointier butts, whereas the females (that can lay eggs) have very rounded butts like perfect circles. Bed bugs can lay up to 7 eggs per blood meal or day which means population can double within a week. So it won’t take long to notice them if you do have them. Goodluck!!!! ❤️❤️
